signals.title: Record $7.9B EUV scanner order from ASML for HBM and DRAM fabs
signals.signal: SK Hynix discloses ~$7.9B (KRW 11.95T) EUV scanner purchase from ASML — the largest single EUV order ever publicly disclosed — covering ~30 machines to be delivered by end-2027 for M15X (HBM) and Yongin (advanced DRAM) fabs.
key_points: ~30 EUV machines (KRW 11.95T) — the largest single EUV order ever publicly disclosed
Deliveries through end-2027, destined for the M15X HBM fab and Yongin advanced DRAM fabs
Locks in scanner allocation ahead of the HBM4 / next-gen DRAM node transitions
signals.why_it_matters: EUV scanner allocation is the hardest capacity constraint in advanced DRAM; an order this size locks in SK Hynix's process roadmap and squeezes competitors' access to ASML's limited output.
signals.chain_link: Deepens SK Hynix's single-vendor dependence on ASML upstream and pulls photomask, pellicle, and fab-construction suppliers into a multi-year build-out.

signals.title: DRAM/NAND/HBM sold out through 2026; Nvidia alone is ~24% of sales
signals.signal: SK Hynix confirms full sell-out of DRAM, NAND, and HBM capacity through 2026, primarily driven by Nvidia, and reports Nvidia alone accounted for ~24% (KRW 23.26T, ~$17.6B) of total 2025 sales; SK Hynix also secures ~70% of Nvidia's HBM4 orders for the Vera Rubin platform.
key_points: All DRAM, NAND, and HBM capacity fully committed through 2026
Nvidia accounted for ~24% of 2025 revenue (KRW 23.26T, ~$17.6B)
SK Hynix secured ~70% of Nvidia's HBM4 orders for the Vera Rubin platform
signals.why_it_matters: Guaranteed volume and pricing power for two years — but revenue concentration this deep makes Nvidia's roadmap and order timing the single biggest swing factor in SK Hynix's P&L.
signals.chain_link: Ties SK Hynix's downstream fortunes to the Nvidia platform ecosystem: hyperscaler cloud capex and AI-server OEM build rates now set its demand signal.

signals.title: First to HBM4 mass production, with a roadmap through HBM5E
signals.signal: SK Hynix announces world's first HBM4 mass-production readiness (Sep 2025), ships 12-layer HBM4 samples to customers (Mar 2025), and ships HBM4E samples to major customers (Jun 2026), while unveiling a multi-generation roadmap (HBM4E → HBM5 → HBM5E, GDDR7-Next, DDR6, 400L+ 4D NAND) at the SK AI Summit 2025.
key_points: World-first HBM4 mass-production readiness declared (Sep 2025); 12-layer samples shipped Mar 2025
HBM4E samples shipped to major customers in Jun 2026
Roadmap unveiled at SK AI Summit 2025: HBM4E → HBM5 → HBM5E, GDDR7-Next, DDR6, 400L+ 4D NAND
signals.why_it_matters: Being first to each HBM generation is what won the Nvidia allocation; the HBM4 base die moves to TSMC's logic foundry, changing SK Hynix's cost structure and partner risk.
signals.chain_link: Adds TSMC as a critical upstream partner (base die + CoWoS packaging) and raises the stakes for advanced packaging materials and MR-MUF thermal suppliers.

signals.title: $3.87B Indiana advanced-packaging fab breaks ground
signals.signal: SK Hynix breaks ground on its $3.87B advanced packaging (2.5D) fab in West Lafayette, Indiana (Apr 2026), targeting HBM4E/HBM5 production in 2H 2028, with $458M in US CHIPS Act funding and a collaboration with Purdue University; simultaneously investing KRW 19T in a new Cheongju packaging fab (P&T7).
key_points: 2.5D advanced-packaging fab in West Lafayette, Indiana targeting HBM4E/HBM5 output in 2H 2028
$458M in US CHIPS Act funding plus a Purdue University collaboration
Parallel KRW 19T investment in a new Cheongju packaging fab (P&T7) in Korea
signals.why_it_matters: SK Hynix's first US production footprint de-risks geopolitics for its US customers and anchors CHIPS-funded packaging capacity next to the customer base.
signals.chain_link: Creates a new US demand center for equipment makers (Applied Materials, Lam Research), specialty gas/chemical suppliers, and substrate vendors who must localize support.

signals.title: HBM3E contract prices raised ~20% for 2026 supply
signals.signal: SK Hynix and Samsung raise HBM3E contract prices by ~20% for 2026 supply, driven by tightening capacity as both vendors prioritize HBM4 ramps; demand surge attributed to Nvidia H200 China re-export approvals plus new ASIC-based HBM3E designs from Google TPU v7 and Amazon Trainium3.
key_points: SK Hynix and Samsung both raised 2026 HBM3E contract prices by ~20%
Capacity tightening as both vendors prioritize HBM4 ramps
Demand boosted by Nvidia H200 China re-export approvals and new ASIC designs (Google TPU v7, Amazon Trainium3)
signals.why_it_matters: Direct margin expansion on the legacy HBM line while HBM4 ramps — and evidence that ASIC customers are now a price-setting demand block alongside Nvidia.
signals.chain_link: Broadens downstream demand from a single GPU customer to custom-ASIC designers and their co-design partner Broadcom, plus resellers and pricing analysts tracking allocation.

signals.title: Ex-CEO Seok-Hee Lee joins Intel to lead advanced packaging
signals.signal: Former SK Hynix CEO Seok-Hee Lee hired by Intel as EVP to lead Intel Foundry's advanced packaging division (Jun 2026), directly overseeing EMIB-T and HBI technologies — occurring as SK Hynix is reportedly testing Intel's EMIB packaging for HBM integration; simultaneously, SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh-Jung was reappointed (Mar 2025) with a term through 2028.
key_points: Lee named Intel EVP over Intel Foundry's advanced packaging (EMIB-T, HBI) in Jun 2026
SK Hynix is reportedly testing Intel's EMIB packaging for HBM integration
Current CEO Kwak Noh-Jung reappointed (Mar 2025) with a term through 2028
signals.why_it_matters: A senior knowledge transfer to a potential packaging partner-slash-rival — Intel Foundry clearly wants HBM-class packaging business, which could open a second-source path or leak process know-how.
signals.chain_link: Creates a possible new anchor-level tie between SK Hynix HBM and Intel Foundry packaging, alongside the existing TSMC CoWoS dependence.

signals.title: 2025 capex raised ~32% to KRW 29T; KRW 1,100T cluster master plan
signals.signal: SK Hynix raises 2025 capex guidance to KRW 29T (from KRW 22T original target, ~+32%), driven by HBM equipment investments; also announces KRW 1,100T (~$800B) ultra-long-term fab cluster plan spanning Yongin, Cheongju, and a new Southwestern Region cluster, with the Yongin fourth fab now accelerated to 2033 completion.
key_points: 2025 capex guidance lifted from KRW 22T to KRW 29T (~+32%), driven by HBM equipment
KRW 1,100T (~$800B) ultra-long-term fab cluster plan spanning Yongin, Cheongju, and a new Southwestern cluster
Yongin fourth fab accelerated to 2033 completion
signals.why_it_matters: A one-third capex raise mid-year is a hard cash-flow commitment to the AI-memory cycle, and the multi-decade cluster plan sets the ceiling for Korea's memory supply growth.
signals.chain_link: A demand wave for the entire upstream equipment complex — Tokyo Electron, inspection/metrology vendors, and wafer suppliers SUMCO and Shin-Etsu all size against this plan.

signals.title: First HBM3E supplier for Google's Ironwood TPU
signals.signal: SK Hynix confirms it is the first HBM3E supplier for Google's Ironwood TPU and its upcoming v7p/v7e TPUs; Google TPU customers (Nvidia, Google, Amazon) collectively account for ~30% of SK Hynix HBM revenue, establishing a strategic second anchor outside Nvidia as Google expands TPU sales to Meta and others.
key_points: Confirmed first HBM3E supplier for Google's Ironwood TPU and the upcoming v7p/v7e
Nvidia, Google, and Amazon together account for ~30% of SK Hynix HBM revenue
Google is expanding TPU sales to Meta and others, growing the non-Nvidia demand anchor
signals.why_it_matters: Establishes a strategic second demand anchor outside Nvidia, cutting single-customer risk just as TPU volumes scale to external buyers.
signals.chain_link: Adds the Google/Broadcom TPU co-design ecosystem and AI-infrastructure end-users (Meta, enterprise) as first-class downstream nodes next to the Nvidia platform.
